decision: read-only qrexec resource probe plus bounded concurrent calibration harness

reviews.preferred: measure worker-Qube RAM and CPU from /proc and bind samples to git SHA, topology, run and capability profile
reviews.reason: planning constants cannot prove deployability; collector-compatible measured evidence can

reviews.preferred: dedicated read-only qrexec probe with strict JSON schema, explicit service name and bounded timeouts
reviews.reason: avoids shell-command injection, mutation authority and a long-lived telemetry daemon

reviews.preferred: concurrent per-round probes with bounded sample count and interval
reviews.reason: keeps samples temporally comparable while adding only read-only qrexec calls and no production worker state changes

alternatives.lesson: lowest cost but cannot validate real Qubes resource pressure
higher fidelity at scale but adds lifecycle, credentials, storage, attack surface and background resource cost
would increase privileged integration surface and couples qualification to dom0 command execution

winner.robustness: fail-closed parsing, bounded probes, provenance-bound collector contract
winner.latency: one read-only qrexec probe per worker per round; workers sampled concurrently
winner.resourceUse: no daemon/database; short CPU sampling window and bounded rounds
winner.regressionRisk: new calibration-only files; no MissionQueue/coordinator mutation semantics changed
winner.qa: unit tests cover /proc parsing, guest CPU accounting, concurrency/order, qrexec invocation, collector compatibility and malformed inputs

failuresAndLessons: Initial CPU accounting summed guest/guest_nice although Linux already includes them in user/nice; corrected to user..steal fields before adoption.
Measured calibration is evidence only after samples are collected in real Qubes; fixtures must not be called real resource qualification.
Hosted CI remains a separate release gate and local/model review does not replace it.
